current_activity: Capture of Stuttgart: a French column breaks into the city from the northeast
notes: Event date: 21 April 1945 (CMH The Last Offensive, p. 429: the boundary change of the 20th, then the next day; the city clear on 22 April); Wikipedia gives April 1945 for the division. Event definition: The division takes part in the assault and capture of Stuttgart; a French column envelops the city by Esslingen and breaks into its northeastern fringe on 21 April, and the city is clear on 22 April. Event support: three source families (Wikipedia, the US Army official history (CMH) and de Lattre's History of the French First Army). Wikipedia, 5th Armored Division (France), section World War II: "The 5th Armored Division particularly distinguished itself in the assault and capture of Stuttgart, Germany in April 1945"; CMH The Last Offensive ch. 18 p. 429: "General Devers on the 20th legitimatized the French foray into the Seventh Army's zone by a change in the interarmy boundary, whereupon a French column the next day pushed down the valley of the Neckar by way of Esslingen, enveloped Stuttgart, and broke into the northeastern fringe of the city early in the afternoon"; "The following day, 22 April, Stuttgart was clear"; de Lattre, The History of the French First Army (1952) p. 460-466: "when Stuttgart fell on the 21st April". Location: Stuttgart, Baden-Württemberg with a precision of 10 km. Location support: Wikipedia names Stuttgart for the division; the CMH history dates the French column to 21 April without naming the division, so the attribution of the date to the division is an inferred value and confidence stays 0.3. French follow-up: the date was checked and confirmed against p. 429 (unchanged, 21 April). French follow-up (de Lattre): de Lattre (pp. 460-466) dates the fall of Stuttgart to 21 April, in the pages his notes summarise as the 5th DB's rush along the Neckar to Stuttgart; the day now rests on two source families (CMH, de Lattre), the city on three, while the link of the day to this division still rests on the note's summary rather than on its quote, so confidence is raised from 0.3 to 0.5, not to 0.7. Activity: in_line, span point, inferred; in the activity rollout, Canada and France (October 2026), the old value of activity_status is blank, the new value is in_line (point, inferred); reason: the cited source describes part of the division (a brigade, battalion, combat command, column, patrol or advance detachment) in action on this date; the main body is taken to be in the line with it, so the value is inferred.
